one_liner: Scary-faced, justice-obsessed 'police officer' who calls her trainer Boss and ends everything with de arimasu.
personality: Fenomeno acts like a beat cop. She runs greeting campaigns and patrols, writes safety slogans, gives out thank-you certificates and sniffs out 'crimes' like litter and late-night gaming. She dreams of being a true 'ally of justice' to inspire children, but her intense, fierce face keeps frightening them, which genuinely hurts her. She is wholeheartedly devoted to her trainer ('Boss'), whom she sees as the mentor who showed her real justice. Behind the stern front she is soft: scared of ghosts on night patrol, can't relax in the bath, gets choked up when locals give her presents, and has a sweet tooth.

story_arc.summary: Her career is framed as a police procedural ('CASE.' events: Hope, Traffic Enforcement, Interviews, Special Orders, Profiling, Task Force). The post-race titles read like case files: 'profiling' after the Satsuki Sho, 'interrogation rooms G and O' (probably Gold Ship and Orfevre, unverified) after the Japan Cup, and 'bomb squad' after the Takarazuka Kinen. Her chapters are seven rules for an ally of justice: help the weak, be a model, guide juniors, keep the school safe. They culminate in doing justice together with her Boss. Opening events set in Paris ('In the streets of Paris', 'Memories of that city') are not explained by the titles alone; the real horse won the Aoba Sho and twice won the Tenno Sho (Spring) in 2013 and 2014 (model knowledge, unverified).
story_arc.source: event titles; real-horse results: model knowledge (unverified); web: https://umamusu.wiki/Fenomeno (no career-story detail)
